newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-MUSTER TO APPEAL TO INTERNATIONAL TENNIS FEDERATION.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER TO APPEAL TO INTERNATIONAL TENNIS FEDERATION.

text.p: Thomas Muster will join an Austrian delegation at an ITF meeting in London next week to explain their Davis Cup team's walkout from a world group qualifying tie in Brazil this month, the Austrian Tennis Federation (OTV) said on Monday.

OTV general secretary Peter Nader said the International Tennis Federation took the unusual step of inviting representatives from both affected countries to a meeting in London on October 7 to discuss the incident.
"Thomas Muster expressed his wish to attend so we chose him as one of our representatives because he was directly involved in the incident," Nader said.

Muster, Austria's world number three, stormed off the court during the doubles match on September 21 claiming the Brazilian crowd had continually insulted him and his doubles partner, Udo Plamberger, and also spat and threw small stones onto the court.
The Austrian team also pulled out of the reverse singles and flew home a day early, forfeiting the matches and giving Brazil victory by 4-1.

"We don't know what to expect from the meeting. We hope that either the tie can be repeated on neutral ground or that we are handed the victory," Nader said, adding he did not believe the ITF would ban Austria from the Davis Cup competition.
The OTV has prepared a 30-page report criticising the crowd behaviuor in Sao Paulo, the surface of the court and the quality of television coverage.
Other OTV representatives at the ITF meeting will be Nader himself, vice-president Christian Ransmayer and Muster's coach and Davis Cup non-playing caprain ronald Leitgeb.
